column3: “One afternoon” expands the Greek indication of the ninth prayer hour.
The Greek says “from his mother’s womb”; “courts” is supplied.
BSB repeats Peter’s name and divides the shared looking into two clauses.
The Greek joins silver and gold with “and,” rather than “or.”
“Peter” makes the unnamed subject explicit; the Greek says he raised him.
“Courts” is supplied; the Greek explicitly says he stood.
The Greek repeats “God” before Isaac and Jacob; “even though” interprets the participial relation.
The Greek makes His name the subject that strengthened the man in the first clause; BSB makes the man passive and then repeats the name in the next clause.
The Greek explicitly refers to the mouth of the prophets.
The Greek says plural “times” and preserves the image of the prophets’ mouth.
The Greek calls the person a “soul” and explicitly repeats “that prophet”; “his” is not separately stated before people.
